newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sets $2 bln foreign loan ceiling for firms.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sets $2 bln foreign loan ceiling for firms.

text.p: South Korea has set a $2 billion foreign loan ceiling for companies to purchase domestically-made equipments next year, the Ministry of Economy and Finance said on Monday.
A ministry statement said firms buying more than 50 percent of their planned machinery purchases from domestic manufacturers would be eligible to apply for foreign loans.
The measure was aimed at helping domestic companies that have been suffering from high costs and low management efficiency to improve their competitiveness, the statement said.
The ministry has also put a $1 billion foreign loan ceiling for companies in high technology industries to finance imports of capital goods in 1997.
The 15 provincial and metropolitan city governments would also be allowed to borrow up to $500 million in foreign loans next year to finance infrastructure projects, the statement added.
